strategies.name: Lean
strategies.description: Keep inputs light. Accept more uncovered demand to limit surplus.

policy_parameters.description: Keep inputs light. Accept more uncovered demand to limit surplus.

objective_terms.unit: SGD-equivalent policy utility; coefficients are declared preferences, not forecast costs

solver.integer_units: grams, cents/kg, minutes, whole beds; scenario weights normalized to 1000 integer units

assumptions: Synthetic recipes and declared scenarios; not commercial yield validation.
Scenario weights are validated, normalized and consumed by the weighted objective. No random scenario sampling is performed.
Fresh marketable yield includes packout once.
Future sowing cannot cover earlier deliveries.
Order service uses booked-before-residual, then known higher price and stable ID because buyer/grade priority fields are absent.
Closing stock remains physical inventory with zero salvage value and a declared policy penalty; it is not counted as waste.
SGD cost fixture: labour 12/hour, packing 0.30/kg delivered, disposal 0.15/kg.

risk.basis: reported minimum across declared scenarios; not a calibrated quantile

claims.statement: Across the feasible strategies, booked-order deliveries fall short of booked requested quantity, and each strategy also leaves residual requested demand undelivered; declared violations are absent, which means no hard-constraint breach was reported, not that demand is covered.

Frozen synthetic strategy metrics and declared violation context are available; no declared hard-constraint violation was reported for any strategy, which does not establish demand coverage or absence of unmodelled constraints.
No connected community source supplies grower or buyer reactions, so no demand or price interpretation is supported; booked weighted averages are synthetic order inputs, not observed prices.

All supplied strategies carry no declared hard-constraint violation, and each scheduled crop batch lists a sowing, transplant and harvest date consistent with its recipe, so the frozen plan is internally feasible under declared constraints. This does not establish demand coverage, which the fill rates show remains partial, nor the absence of unmodelled constraints.

Frozen schedule facts show batch sow, transplant and harvest dates ordered consistently with the lead-time rule, and booked-order shortfalls appear only on later-dated orders; earlier-dated residual orders show delivery matching request. No declared hard violation is reported for any strategy, so feasibility status reflects only declared constraints, not demand coverage or unmodelled logistics.

All strategies are feasible with no declared hard-constraint violations, and frozen synthetic metrics show each is margin-positive under booked weighted-average price assumptions rather than observed market prices; margins differ across strategies but the evidence does not establish any ranking basis.

Each strategy carries no declared hard-constraint violation, so selection follows the stated policy: prefer Balanced among feasible strategies, not an invented ranking. Feasibility reflects declared constraints only, not demand coverage or unmodelled limits.
